comparator.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: Current route catalogue confirms 60 EC each year. In year three, the 30-EC taught and research allocation comprises one 10-EC exploration course, the 15-EC thesis project and 5 EC of professional impact. The separate 30-EC choice space remains open. Tutoring has no separate credit, and first-year tutoring is part of the positive study advice requirement. Current module admissions establish the sequence from first-year research and academic skills through second-year preparation and fieldwork, then the thesis, exploration and professional impact requirements.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The target is the generic bachelor. Both specialisations share the first year and the same total credit weight. Leiden presents People, Planet, Power first in its public programme structure, so this route is selected independently of UCR fit. Anthropology of Religion is the first option in the selected route’s 10-EC exploration group.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad route covers cultural difference, development, power and qualitative inquiry. The ecology route responds to the People, Planet, Power direction. The visual culture route responds to the media and representation strand of Media, Making, Movements, with digital ethnography remaining a gap. All three schedules are feasible and pairwise distinct.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce systematic theoretical study of society and social organisation, although Leiden provides a dedicated anthropology-and-sociology sequence.
Both situate cultural and social change historically and transnationally.
Both develop qualitative research design, interviewing, observation, analysis and interpretation; Leiden adds dedicated anthropological field practice.
Both examine modern social theory, diversity, inequality and changing social relations.
Both engage advanced social theory about power, inequality and contemporary societies.
The historical research paper develops a research question, source criticism and sustained argument. Leiden requires a distinct anthropology thesis.
Both use comparison to examine human communities and cultural difference, while archaeology and anthropology retain distinct methods.
UCR qualitative-methods study does not reproduce Leiden's separately credited ethnographic fieldwork component.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Leiden's multivariate-analysis component.
Both analyse states, citizenship, political institutions and power.
Governance cases connect institutions, power and collective environmental decisions. Leiden approaches these relations through anthropological political economy.
Rhetorical argument, writing and speaking provide partial preparation for disciplinary writing in anthropology.
Ethical argument supports reflection on research responsibilities. Leiden also teaches practical ethics and data handling for ethnography.
Both develop regionally grounded cultural analysis, though with distinct disciplinary objects and methods.
Both use mediated and visual forms to analyse and communicate social life.
Data preparation and visualisation in R are shared quantitative skills. Leiden teaches statistical analysis for anthropology and sociology.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Anthropology of Religion.
Academic reading and writing are distributed across the UCR programmes.
Both support reflection on academic development, professional identity and future pathways.
No single selected UCR course is presented as a direct counterpart to Leiden's specialisation-specific research preparation.
Leiden's genuine 30-EC elective space remains open and is not replaced by invented content.

notes.text: Leiden’s dedicated anthropology degree includes sequenced theory, ethnographic methods and fieldwork. At UCR, sociology, qualitative inquiry and related subjects offer a different combination of these interests.
Leiden reserves 30 EC in year three for approved elective choices, which can include a minor, exchange or eligible internship.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology degree studies cultural difference, inequality and social change through theory and field research. Students start with a common first year, then choose People, Planet, Power or Media, Making, Movements.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR routes connect sociology and qualitative research with global change, environmental governance or visual culture. They offer related study alongside gaps in dedicated anthropology theory, sequenced ethnographic fieldwork, digital ethnography and the Leiden thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC shown include the People, Planet, Power specialisation, one 10-EC exploration choice and 30 EC of open elective space. Tutoring carries no separate credits. First-year tutoring is required for positive study advice.

componentNotes.y2-fieldwork: Pass the required first-year writing, research, ethics and statistics courses. Pass both research design contributions before starting the three-week January fieldwork. Tutorials, lectures and the closing conference are compulsory.
componentNotes.y2-research-preparation: The first-year research, ethics, writing and statistics requirements also apply to this preparation course.
componentNotes.y2-multivariate: Finish the Fieldwork NL research period and pass the required first-year courses before starting multivariate analysis.
componentNotes.y3-religion: One of the two 10-EC exploration options in this specialisation. Entry requires completion of the first year, Research Preparation, Fieldwork NL and both specialisation Key Issues courses.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: The 15-EC project combines thematic preparation, a proposal and an individual thesis. Entry requires the completed first year, Diversity and Power and at least one Key Issues course specific to the specialisation.
componentNotes.y3-impact: Complete the first- and second-year Academic Skills and Research Lab courses and Diversity and Power before registering.
componentNotes.y3-electives: The 30 EC may be used for approved electives, a minor, exchange or eligible internship arrangements. The allocation does not prescribe a particular package.
